description: Cosmic Scholars is a team dedicated to designing a new and unique way for young space lovers to explore space exploration.
summary:
Our project involves an interactive and informative game catered towards a younger audience, which allows them to engage through fun and enjoyable gameplay while also learning about the decision making skills required on an actual Martian Outpost while utilizing real life data to simulate conditions on Mars. The user plays as an astronaut, who is awaiting rescue on a failing Martian Outpost. The game has interactive visuals , while also being informative at the same time through the use of accurate data from NASA's DONKI API. This helps to solve the major problem regarding content for a younger audience allowing them to actually experience what it is like to be an astronaut on Mars, while keeping learning fun.

THE PROJECT IS PUT AS A ".exe" FILE ON GITHUB AND MUST BE DOWNLOADED WITH ITS ".pck" FILE TO FUNCTION PROPERLY.
details:
Our project allows young audiences to learn how to operate a Martian Outpost through the use of key decision making skills all of which have consequences, for example Radiation Shielding may protect you against radiation but also reduce power. It does this through the use of an interactive 3D game where the player works as a control room operator on a Martian Outpost being on the lookout for any dangerous events occuring and responding to them in adequate time by activating certain things like Radiation Shielding, Air Filteration or Retract Solar Panels otherwise hazards like Toxic Perchlorates and Radiation will build up which hurt the player and kill it if not kept below certain thresholds. The game has a survival based objective where the player must make it through the number of days (configureable from 5-30) in order to win; the difficulty of the game increases every day uptill day 5 with each day introducing new resources to worry about and new dangerous events. It also has infinite replayability as the events are completely randomized through the use of NASA's DONKI API with the project fetching data from randomized dates from the API allowing for each day to be completely unique and present a brand new challenge!

The project is beneficial to young learners as it allows them to engage in the world of space through a fun and entertaining game while also being informative and teaching them about the critical skills that are required for operating such outposts on another planet and allow them to understand the consequences of failing to do manage resources properly providing for an excellent learning opportunity.

Our team evaluated several factors of the game making process in order to make it engaging and also informative. We did a thorough overview of the UI in order to make it as appealing as possible and the user engagement through the use of buttons. We also considered the severity of each dangerous event through the use of NASA's API and our own understanding connecting it to a radiation and toxic perchlorates bar in order to make it as accurate as possible depending on the severity and evaluated the impact of everything on the power that the space station is exerting. We also evaluated the impact that each hazard on the health of the player making it as accurate as possible.

We used the Godot Engine (4.7 Version) in order to make the game as it is perfectly compatible for making browser games and relatively easy to use. We used the in-built programming language of Godot called "GD Script" in order to write the code used in the game and create the UI interface. The project was compiled on GitHub where all of its source code is visible and the executeable file of the game is available on their as well. Canva was used in order to create the design for the presentation. There was some usage of the AI chatbot "Claude" for code and debugging. THE PROJECT IS PUT AS A ".exe" FILE ON GITHUB AND MUST BE DOWNLOADED WITH ITS ".pck" FILE TO FUNCTION PROPERLY.

The intended impact of our project is to allow passionate young learners to explore the world of human settlement on Mars while keeping them entertained so they don't get bored and keep the content informative and understandable so they actually learn something; compared to other games which either make the information too hard for young players to understand or oversimply it too much so that they don't learn anything at all!
